findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||
findings.body: The authorization gate `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...));` requires the user to be BOTH admin AND owner. The intent is admin OR owner (typical permission check). Using `&&` means an admin who isn't an owner (or vice-versa) cannot add guests, and only true owners who are also admins ever satisfy it. This is a high-impact auth regression for team bookings.

findings.title: Email deduplication is case-sensitive, lets same data form differently-typed duplicates through
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails with case-sensitive string comparison (`guest === attendee.email`, `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). The blacklist is lowercased, but incoming `guest` strings are not. RFC 5321 in practice treats the domain as case-insensitive and most providers treat the local part as case-insensitive too. Submitting `Foo@Bar.com` and an existing attendee `foo@bar.com` (or a blacklisted `FOO@bar.com`) is treated as a new guest, allowing duplicates and bypassing the blacklist. Same issue exists in `apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx` (Set-based uniqueness on the raw values) and in `packages/emails/email-manager.ts` (`newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`), which causes newly added guests to receive the wrong email variant.

findings.title: No transaction around DB update and external calendar call
findings.body: `prisma.booking.update` adds the new attendees to the DB, and only then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is called against external calendars with no try/catch or transaction wrapper. If the calendar sync throws (network failure, auth, daily/zoom error), the booking now has new attendees persisted while the underlying video/calendar provider never received them, and the user sees no error and no rollback. Wrap the DB update and the external calendar update in a compensating action (or catch and roll back attendees) so failures don't leave the system in an inconsistent state.

findings.title: Emails sent to blacklisted guests because original `guests` array is used
findings.body: The handler filters blacklisted emails into `uniqueGuests`, but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the unfiltered input. If a user submits a mix containing at least one valid guest, blacklisted addresses in the same submission still get email notifications (and may even receive a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` depending on how `attendees.includes(attendee.email)` resolves). Send notifications to `uniqueGuests` (or at minimum exclude blacklisted ones) and consider lowercasing before comparison.

findings.title: Existing attendees can add arbitrary guests to someone else's meeting
findings.body: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find(a => a.email === user.email)` makes any person on the original booking authorized to add guests. There is no restriction on which guests (e.g., it could be anyone on the internet, including the organizer's competitors, third parties unrelated to the event, or used for spam/phishing). This is a privilege escalation: invitees are not the booking owner. If attendees adding guests is intentional, it should at least be limited (e.g., max count, requires confirmation, recorded in audit log, etc.); otherwise the authorization model should be reduced to organizer/team-admin/owner only.

findings.title: Misleading TRPCError message for empty uniqueGuests
findings.body: When `uniqueGuests.length === 0`, the handler throws `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`. The real cause is that all submitted addresses were either duplicates of existing attendees or blacklisted (or the list was empty). The message implies a format/duplicate validation problem to the caller and to the toast in the dialog, which is misleading. Use a message that reflects the actual condition (e.g., `no_new_guests_to_add`) and return a more accurate HTTP/UI message.

findings.title: No booking state check (cancelled, past, recurring) before mutating
findings.body: The handler never inspects `booking.status` or `booking.endTime`. This allows adding guests to CANCELLED, REJECTED, or already-finished bookings (and to recurring-event members without scoping). The action should be restricted to upcoming, non-cancelled bookings; if recurring, the implementation should either disallow or apply to the full series intentionally. Otherwise users can add guests to events that already occurred.

findings.title: Subject uses attendees[0].name, crashes if attendees is empty and ignores others
findings.body: `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` if `attendees` is empty (and the catch in the handler swallows the email error so the failure is silent). Additionally, only the first attendee's name is used even when many are present; the booking confirmation pattern elsewhere usually renders a multi-attendee list. Defensively handle an empty array and consider using a list of attendee names or the organizer/team context.

findings.title: Newly added attendees may receive AttendeeAddGuestsEmail instead of confirmation
findings.body: `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` is case-sensitive, but `attendee.email` (from DB, typically lowercased) and the submitted `newGuests` strings can differ in case. A newly added guest whose email case does not exactly match will be sent the "guests added" notification instead of the full booking confirmation email — which is the opposite of what they need. The whole check, plus the client/server dedup, must be case-insensitive (lowercase before compare) so the correct email goes to each.

findings.title: Validation schema rebuilt each render; dedup is case-sensitive; error never clears on edit
findings.body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is constructed inside the component on every render (also: the inner `refine` deduplicates with a case-sensitive `Set`). Beyond perf, the dedup allows case-variant duplicates through. More importantly, when validation fails, `isInvalidEmail` is set to true and only reset on Cancel; subsequent keystrokes that fix the input don't clear the red error banner, so the user sees a stale failure even after correcting the email. Clear the error in `setValue`/`MultiEmail` change handler and lowercase before comparing.

findings.title: Submits empty-string entries if user clicks Add without filling the seeded input
findings.body: Initial state is `[""]` and the validation runs on the full array (including empty entries). The zod `.email()` rejects empty strings, so the user gets a generic "emails must be unique and valid" error and can't tell that the cause is the blank seeded input. Strip empty strings before validation, or include a clear inline message that distinguishes empty/invalid/duplicate.

findings.title: "add_members" action is shown unconditionally for every editable booking
findings.body: The new action is added to `editBookingActions` for all bookings shown through the Edit menu, regardless of booking status, start time, or whether the viewer is organizer/admin/owner. While the server enforces permissions, the UI still surfaces a "Add guests" action that, for past or cancelled bookings, will fail (since the new handler doesn't guard against these states). Also, the action id `add_members` is misleading — it adds guests, not members.

findings.title: Component mutates its `value` prop directly
findings.body: `value = value || [];` reassigns the incoming prop. In React this silently breaks the source state contract (e.g., parent state can diverge from what the component is rendering, effects/memos based on `value` may not fire correctly, and linters/Hooks rules flag it). Use a local alias (`const safeValue = value ?? [];`) and never reassign props.

findings.title: Hardcoded `required` on every email input
findings.body: Every rendered `EmailField` passes `required` unconditionally. This makes form-level validation impossible (HTML form submission will always be blocked) and is also misleading for the "add another" UX where users can intentionally leave the new field blank while editing another. Drop the hardcoded `required`, or scope it to form contexts.

findings.title: No max length on guests list, enables unbounded inserts/emails
findings.body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)`. A caller can submit arbitrarily large arrays, triggering many DB inserts, many calendar API calls inside `updateCalendarAttendees`, and many emails. Add a reasonable max (e.g., 20-50) in the schema and a per-user rate limit on the mutation.

findings.title: Email sending errors silently swallowed, user told "Guests added"
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` is wrapped in try/catch with only `console.log`. On failure the dialog still shows the success toast and the mutation returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the organizer believes every attendee was notified when in fact some may not have been. Either surface the error or only show success after both DB and email pipelines succeed.

findings.title: No tests for the new addGuests handler/schema/dialog
findings.body: The PR adds a new TRPC mutation (`addGuests`) with non-trivial authorization logic (team admin/owner, organizer, attendee), email blacklist filtering, case-sensitivity, calendar sync, and two new email templates, plus a new dialog component — and ships no tests. Given the auth/duplicate/blacklist bugs visible above, this is a substantial test gap. Add unit tests for the handler (authorization matrix, blacklist, duplicates, case-insensitivity, cancelled/past bookings) and integration/component tests for `AddGuestsDialog` validation paths.
